Jane — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the detailed redline. Appreciated.

High level response: we are open to a protection mechanism but want to avoid an open-ended rebate that creates runaway exposure. Proposed go-forward:
- Redwood can accept a quarterly true-up tied to actual usage vs committed baseline, capped at a single one-time credit equal to the pro-rated difference for up to 3 months of committed spend (not 6).
- The credit will not exceed $50,000 per 12-month period (cap applies across invoices).
- Exclusions: planned shutdowns (customer written notice >=60 days), force majeure, and acquisitions/divestitures are excluded from true-up calculations.
- If Nimbus requires a longer runway in the first year (e.g., ramp risk), we can add a one-time ramp credit of up to $20k tied to documented onboarding milestones.

We will return a redline showing those positions; Marissa (legal) and Aditya (account) will weigh in on the exact trigger language. If those caps are a non-starter, let us know which elements are essential so we can prioritize.

Next steps: I will send a redlined appendix with tracked changes and a short summary of changes by EOD Friday. If you need something sooner, we can escalate.

Team — forwarding Nimbus' redline. Quick internal position for negotiating with Procurement:

Quoted: 
On Wed, Dec 2, 2026 at 9:14 AM Nimbus Contracts <contracts@nimbushealth.com> wrote:
> Attached is our redline ... our legal has inserted language to allow a quarterly true-up ... a one-time rebate equal to the difference up to 6 months of committed spend.

My suggested play (short):
- Accept a quarterly true-up but limit the rebate exposure to 3 months of committed spend and a hard dollar cap of $50k. That protects them while giving Redwood predictable exposure.
- Require 60 days' written notice for any intentional decommission that would materially reduce baseline (to prevent retroactive churn).
- Define Force Majeure narrowly and explicitly exclude customer-initiated product retirement and M&A (we do not want to eat those costs).
- Add a "ramp" pathway: first 90 days post-commencement counted as ramp; reductions inside that window will be treated separately (one-time onboarding credit up to $20k).
- Add a clause that any credit triggers automatic re-evaluation of minimum committed bands but does not change the per-token price mid-term (no retroactive price resets outside true-up credit).

Marissa — can you propose concise legal wording for: (A) the dollar cap, (B) the 60-day notice carveout, and (C) how to tie the credit calculation (percent delta vs baseline vs absolute token counts)? Keep it defensible in procurement redlines (they will push for broader MFN-like language).

Aditya — if we accept the $50k cap, will that materially change deal economics / commission structure? If so, we might need to split the ramp credit differently.

Thanks — goal is a single redline back to them with explanation bullets and our preferred DocuSign link.

— Olga

Reply (Marissa):
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:34:00 -0800

Olga — suggested legal language below (short versions you can paste into the appendix):
1) Dollar cap and credit: "Customer True-Up Credit: If Customer's actual monthly usage in any rolling 90-day period is at least 35% lower than the agreed committed baseline, Customer may request a one-time True-Up Credit up to the lesser of (a) the pro-rated difference in fees accrued for up to three (3) months of committed spend, or (b) USD $50,000. Any True-Up Credit granted will be netted against Customer's next invoice and does not constitute a refund."
2) Notice carveout: "Planned decommissions are excluded from True-Up calculation provided Customer delivers written notice at least sixty (60) calendar days prior to the effective decommission date; such notice must reference impacted services and expected timelines."
3) Calculation method: "True-Up shall be calculated by comparing actual billed units to the committed baseline expressed in monthly units. The committed baseline will be the average of the first three (3) billing months following contract commencement, unless the parties agree in writing to an alternative baseline within thirty (30) days of commencement."

Marissa — flagged procurement will try to expand the credit to refunds and to link to price resets. We should push language that the credit is the exclusive remedy for usage shortfall and explicitly disallows a per-token price change as a substitute.

Aditya — any customer success or finance concerns?

Summary of material changes we propose:
- True-Up Credit: Accepted in principle; capped at the lesser of three (3) months' pro-rated committed spend or USD $50,000 (single credit per 12-month period).
- Exclusions: Planned decommissions (>=60 days' written notice), force majeure, and M&A carveouts explicitly excluded from True-Up triggers.
- Ramp Support: One-time onboarding ramp credit up to USD $20,000 tied to milestone acceptance (detailed in SOW).
- Calculation: Baseline defined as average of first three billing months post-commencement unless otherwise agreed in writing.
- Remedy exclusivity: True-Up credit is the exclusive monetary remedy for usage shortfall; does not permit retroactive per-token price reductions or refunds beyond the defined credit.
